headline: Coupled structure prediction and physics sampling drive new biomolecular binder design
label: Computational Biomolecular Design Methods
summary: Recent preprints report full-length antibody design, miniprotein binders, and epitope-truncated workflows that cut GPU cost.
synthesis: The dominant thread is coupling structure prediction and physics-based sampling with optimization or learning to design or score biomolecular interactions. UnibindMD chains BindCraft design, AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 prediction, PRODIGY affinity, ADMET-AI profiling, and 100 ns MD to validate de novo peptide binders, while Pythia-1 generates full-length IgG antibodies for 22 targets, including GPCR agonists and antagonists. Several preprints modify the search itself: simplex-projected gradient descent replaces softmax-logit optimisation in hallucination-based binder design, and epitope excision truncates targets to interface windows, reducing RFdiffusion and AlphaFold3 GPU time by about 88%. Reinforcement learning appears in FragDockRL and AbOptimizer, and P-RISE identifies force field, ionic, dielectric and entropy requirements for RNA-ligand prediction. Newer work emphasizes integrating design, prediction, and validation within a single workflow, as Astrolabe's closed-loop framework does.
